title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1986 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)'. This is an axiomatic attempt at 'tame topology'. 'Lieux' (loci) form a set L. A 'figure' F is a stratification by finitely many pairwise disjoint pieces, with set of strata F~. F' << F means F' is a refinement of F, and F|X is the figure induced on a sub-figure X. F || G means the figures are disjoint (separated), and Sup denotes the coarsest common refinement.

End of Corollary 2 (started on p.69): F is covered by an admissible family of sub-figures F_i. Suppose we are given a family of refinements F'_i << F_i that is compatible on overlaps (Grothendieck notes 'définition à trouver'). Then there exists a refinement F' of F, necessarily unique, with F'|F_i = F'_i for all i. When I is finite this already follows from a single axiom (read as Ax 4' or similar). In modern terms, X |-> Raff(X) behaves like a sheaf of sets on the poset of sub-figures for admissible coverings. The gluing was constructed on p.69 as F' = Sup of the F'_Z, with underlying set obtained by gluing the sets F'~_X.

Corollary 3, the special case of a disjoint union. Let F, G be figures with F || G, and let H = F ⊔ G be the sum figure.
(i) If F' << F and G' << G, then F' || G' and H' := F' ⊔ G' << H.
(ii) This gives a bijection Raff(F) × Raff(G) -> Raff(F ⊔ G), (F', G') |-> F' ⊔ G'. Its inverse is H' |-> (H'|F, H'|G).
The statement generalises to a figure F that is a disjoint sum of subfamilies F_i, giving Raff(F) ≅ Π_i Raff(F_i).

As a by-product he recovers relation (1.58) of p.59: if F and G are disjoint, F' << F and G' << G, then F' || G'.

Purpose: to set up the formal properties of the refinement poset Raff(F). These are the sheaf property and multiplicativity on sums, which are needed before treating discrete figures (p.71) and further structure.
errors: No mathematical error visible. The notion of a 'compatible' family of refinements is explicitly left undefined ('définition à trouver', p.69), so Cor. 2 is stated somewhat informally.
Minor: (i) asserts F' || G', which is exactly relation (1.58). The page presents (1.58) as recovered at the end, so the logic is slightly circular in presentation, but harmless.

ideas.what: Refinements of a figure glue along an admissible covering by sub-figures, uniquely: Raff behaves as a sheaf on sub-figures.
ideas.modern_name: Sheaf/gluing property of refinements of stratifications (cf. common refinements of cell decompositions in o-minimal geometry)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in o-minimal/semialgebraic geometry (van den Dries and others) for common refinements; no specific credit for this sheaf formulation
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches 'topologie modérée' without such axiomatics

ideas.what: For a disjoint sum of figures, Raff(F ⊔ G) ≅ Raff(F) × Raff(G), with inverse given by restriction.
ideas.modern_name: Multiplicativity of the refinement poset on coproducts

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine formal consequences within Grothendieck's private axiomatics of tame topology (gluing of refinements, product decomposition for disjoint sums). They are of historical interest as part of the unpublished 'analysis situs' project, but contain no mathematically new or uncredited result.
